reason: Sempervirent is the Latin-derived form of evergreen, keeping its leaves all year; PATO_0001733 is the plant-specific term.
A length comparison with a named second part (the corolla), so it is a relation to another part rather than a term.

label: tiered
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a set of structures of the same kind by virtue of their being arranged in superposed horizontal levels.
reason: French 'étagé' covers storied wood rays (in tiers seen in tangential section) and branches in tiers (pagoda-type branching), both arrangement in horizontal levels. No PATO or FLOPO term exists, and only 2 statements support it.

target: new: two values on the hairs as part of the bearer (trichome PO_0000282 + star shaped PATO_0002065 + fascicled FLOPO:0991098; part-of-bearer slot in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md)
reason: The words describe the hairs on the blade or spine, not the organ itself, and combine two values of one hair type. This needs the hair as the part of the bearer, not a new quality.
A part (the scar left by the style on the fruit), not a quality. There is no PO class, and 'scar' was already rejected as a generic part in the previous review.
'Sub-' marks an approximate value of disc-shaped (on stigma and seed). Not FLOPO:0991195 disciform, which is the capitulum type.
'Sub-' marks an approximate value of flabelliform, which the previous review mapped to fan-shaped (rule C227).
French 'subglobuleux' = nearly globose. PATO has the exact term subspherical, which is better than the sub- pattern on spherical.
'Style subnul' = almost nothing, reduced to a trace, read like 'obsolete' (rule C234). 'À l'état sec' (when dry) goes to the specimen-condition pattern.
'Rachis terminé par une vrille' states that the leaf rachis ends in a tendril, which PO has as leaf rachis tendril.
Four-seeded is a count of seeds ('seeded → seed' in flora_counted_parts.tsv). The stamen example ('texsertes') is a transcription error, not this word.

'Tigré' = marked with darker stripes or spots like a tiger. It is used for both, so the shared parent multi-colored is the safe target, not banded or spotted. The colour ('de rouge') is a separate annotation.
Seeds lying in the transverse plane: the same reading as rule C336 for 'transverse'.

target: new: merosity (number of parts in each floral whorl)
reason: Trimerous = floral parts in threes. 03-count-of-parts deliberately does not split '-merous' because it names no single part, so it needs its own count pattern over the whorls.
Trinerved = with three veins, counted with 'nerved → vein'. 'À la base' says they arise at the base, so it is not triplinerved (FLOPO:0991202).
'De longueur inégale' (unequal in length), said of stamens or pappus bristles, is the size quality of a set of like parts that FLOPO:0991101 covers.
French 'unisexuées' = unisexual flowers.

target: docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md (sporangium PO_0025094, count 1; needs a 'sporangiate → sporangium' row in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv)
reason: A sorus or anther with one sporangium is a count of a named part, like '-flowered' and '-seeded'.

target: spur absent (needs a generic spur bearer class; PO has only petal spur PO_0025511 and corolla spur PO_0025512)
reason: 'Non éperonné' = without a spur, so it is the absence of a part, not a quality. The examples are stipules and sepals, for which PO has no spur class, so the rule waits on a bearer class.
It names one indumentum, a short dense soft tomentum with a velvety feel, which is velutinous (EXACT synonym velvety). It is not a mix of two separate values.
Volubile = twining. The definition of climbing explicitly includes growing round a support that the plant twines around.
Acetabuliform = shaped like a shallow cup or saucer (like the acetabulum), which matches saucer-shaped (synonym patelliform).
French 'barbu' = bearded, with a tuft of long hairs (synonym barbate). Not barbed (FLOPO:0991209).
French/variant spelling of basifixed.
The French example 'munis de contreforts ailés' = with winged buttresses. 'Battened' appears to be a mistranslation of that. The bare 'Battened' on a culm is unclear.
Bijugate = with two pairs of leaflets, counted with the 'jugate → leaflet' row in flora_counted_parts.tsv.
'Limbe' (blade) of a leaflet or bract is a part; PO lamina has blade as a synonym. For leaves themselves use leaf lamina PO_0020039.
Short-styled ('brévistylé') flowers are one form of a heterostylous species, and 'brévi ou longistyles' states heterostyly directly. Two statements do not justify a separate short-styled class.
'Maculé de brun' (marked with brown) is the marking pattern plus the colour of the marks. Map the pattern to mottled and annotate brown as a separate colour value.
Bullulate = finely or weakly bullate. The weakening ('weakly', 'sub-') goes in the approximate-value qualifier.
